R3-01.why: Takes the kid reframe the research itself suggested for No Body No Problem! (hide the mess before Mom checks) and the 1vN prank rhythm of Worst Class Ever (#1 Oct Next Fest, strong evidence), so it adapts a principle rather than cloning. The Parent's drive-home lane-dodge phase is a genuinely original fix for the 'hunter idles while hiders set up' problem in 1vN games. Tap-on-highlight hiding and the FREEZE snapshot replace the source's PC physics placement and voice bluffing ('act normal' over proximity chat), so neither precision nor voice is needed. That fits mobile, young players and no-voice play well. Weaknesses: the inspiration evidence is thin (NBNP has no figures and is unreleased). Swapping physics hiding for slot-based hiding drops the physics comedy that made the source fun, which pushes it toward a generic Roblox 1vN hide-and-hunt (Flee the Facility, Piggy and Granny-likes are crowded), with Clean the House as the PvE neighbour. Four phases plus snitch, decoy, gadgets and Gossip cards is a lot of rules for a young first session.
R3-01.fix: Put back one cheap, server-safe physics moment so the source's comedy survives. For example, make a hidden item that sticks out (a TV in the oven with the door ajar) a visible 'tell' the Parent can spot, so hiding quality is about more than which slot you pick. Delay Snitch and Decoy until round 3 or later for new players, and keep the first session to Party, Panic and Hunt with Sniff only.

R3-02.why: The cleanest principle-level adaptation of the set. YAPYAP's 'performative input' (1M sold in 6 weeks) depends on voice, which minors cannot use. Swapping in touch-traced runes keeps the performance, is native to mobile (where touch beats PC), and gets rid of the voice dependency entirely. That is exactly the transfer the research recommends. Magicka-style fusion adds a teamwork hook that works without talking, through the fusion-window glow and the partner-rune icon. Six forgiving runes, a server-side classifier and no thumbstick or camera make the inputs very simple. The nearest Roblox competition is small (Draw Spells Magic Arena, about 615 CCU, PvP), and 'co-op fusion' sets it apart. Risks: the source's laughs come from hearing friends shout and garble spells, and private drawing loses some of that. Misfire comedy (rubber chicken) and big on-screen runes win part of it back. Wave defence also sits next to a saturated Roblox tower-defence space.
R3-02.fix: Kids/Select compliance: never show other players the raw finger trace, because that is free-form drawing. Render only the classified, clean rune glyph and your ink colour. Make the misfires the star of the viral loop (a big name banner and SFX visible to all) to stand in for YAPYAP's shouting. Allow a short buffered fusion window (about 1.5 s, ping-scaled) so mobile players on high ping are not shut out of fusions.

R3-03.why: The inspiration quality is high. Worst Class Ever is the #1 Oct 2026 Next Fest demo, with 300k demo players and a kid-safe theme, and release-to-freeze plus beam-only tagging are smart mobile and lag-tolerant simplifications. Neither voice nor PC precision is needed. But the adaptation sits close to a reskin: shared Mischief meter, NPC blending, a lone hunter and pranks in blind spots all match WCE one for one. WCE launched on Nov 9, and Roblox cloners move in weeks (as with Meccha Chameleon, 150–200k CCU clones), so a 3–4-month build will probably arrive after several WCE-alikes. Be NPC or Die, DISGUISE, In Plain Sight, Prank the Teacher and many Red-Light-Green-Light games already cover the parts. Auto-snapping to a pose also weakens the 'act natural' skill that makes the source fun.
R3-03.fix: Lean into what WCE cannot do and make the statue fantasy carry the identity. For example, statues can carry and stack exhibits to build an escape and the Guard's beam physically stops things, or poses must match the wing's art style for full cover, so blending is a choice and not automatic. Ship faster with a smaller scope (one wing plus 5 pranks) to beat WCE clones. Treat Red Light Green Light as the hook in thumbnails, not WCE.

R3-04.why: Good principle extraction from Fart Together and RV There Yet? (100k CCU, strong): one shared vehicle, one input per player, and one person's mistake becomes everyone's problem. One HOLD button with no thumbstick is the simplest mobile control on the panel and very kid-friendly, and Lookout pings shown as giant arrows replace the voice callouts ('LEFT! LEFT!') the sources lean on. Weaknesses: both sources get their fun from emergent physics plus voice coordination among friends. A kinematic spline raft removes the physics, and coordinating 6 random kids without talking can feel random rather than funny. A direct Roblox competitor already exists (Boat Together, about 8.2M visits, about 2K peak), which shows the demand is modest. The Fart Together source evidence is weak (about 4k CCU demo), and the 13M-visit copy claim is not in my research.
R3-04.fix: Keep a server-side physics-flavoured layer on top of the spline: wobble, tipping and lateral drift that the crew must actively correct, so failures look physical and not scripted. Default matchmaking to 2–4 seats (friends first) and fill empty seats with a competent bot paddler. Make Versus, with its water-bailing sabotage, the headline so the game stands apart from Boat Together.

R3-05.why: The weakest Steam-indie lineage. The inspirations are mostly older or not on Steam (Overcooked 2016, the board game Flash Point, PowerWash 2022, Pet Sim), and Dumpster Gang has no traction figures. That makes it a solid Roblox-native mash-up (firefighting RP plus Rescue Animals' trend, about 20K peak) rather than an adaptation of a current hit. The transfers themselves work: hose magnetism cuts PowerWash's PC precision, downed-teammate drag comes from Dumpster Gang, and the animals suit young players and no-voice co-op. Drag-to-sweep on the right half is reasonable on mobile with a fixed camera. But the system count is high (fire grid, two fire types, tanks and hydrants, critter AI that flees and wriggles, two-player carries, floor collapse, downed state), which is the opposite of simplification. Overcooked's chaos also normally runs on voice callouts, and the concept gives no ping layer to replace them.
R3-05.fix: Cut launch rules to one fire type plus the hose, with critters that run to the nearest player. Add a ping wheel ('critter here', 'need foam', 'help carry') so the Overcooked-style coordination works without voice. To strengthen the Steam angle, borrow one 2025–26 hit principle explicitly, e.g. Mewgenics-style inheritance (rescued critters pair to produce variant companions) as the meta.

overall_notes: Ranking by Steam adaptation: R3-02 > R3-01 > R3-03 = R3-04 > R3-05. R3-02 is the textbook principle-not-clone transfer (voice → touch gesture), and its one fix is a Kids/Select issue: show clean glyphs, never raw traces. R3-01 adapts a weakly evidenced source well and adds an original Parent phase, but it should keep some physics comedy. R3-03 has the strongest source but is too close to Worst Class Ever and will arrive into a wave of WCE clones. R3-04 has the simplest controls but drops the source's physics fun and faces Boat Together. R3-05 is a good Roblox-native idea with weak Steam lineage and too many systems. Across the set, no concept relies on voice or PC precision. Each replaces voice with pings or emotes, which matches the research. The research's best no-voice candidates (BOMBANANA's cyclic sensory roles, Big Walk's communication-as-terrain, Probably Stolen's spot-the-fake) remain unused.
